title: Control Plane field report — weekly (routing/auth/quotas)
body:
Purpose: quick weekly field report from the control-plane channel focused on routing, auth changes, and quota pressure. Intended audience: platform-eng, SRE, and product owners who touch per-route behavior.

Highlights this week:
- Quota bursts: observed two short-lived quota spikes in us-west-2 on 2026-10-14 between 03:10-03:35 UTC. Root cause appears to be a sudden influx of batched small-requests from a customer test harness that retried aggressively when the allocator returned 429s. Peak per-customer token rate hit ~2.3x expected. No customer-facing outage; increased tail latencies for low-priority routes.
- Routing rule regression: a config push (PR #612) added an unintended route tag precedence change for internal telemetry routes. This made some telemetry requests route to dedicated pools rather than the shared pool, causing inefficient capacity usage. Mitigated by rolling back config at 03:47 UTC.
- Auth refresh tokens: new third-party integration (partner X) started returning expanded auth scopes; our token validator rejected the token due to an unexpected claim 'azp_env'. Added a short-term tolerant path in the validator to accept unknown string claims while we coordinate with partner X.

Key metrics snapshot (observed window 2026-10-08 -> 2026-10-15):
- 99th p50 latency (all-hosted text generation): 210ms (target 200ms)
- Token throughput (global): 42M tokens/day (projected 1.3B/mo)
- 5xx rate (control plane): 0.04% (target <0.1%)
- Quota throttles: 1.1k events this week; 68% attributed to automated test clients

What we changed / experiments in flight:
- Autoscaler refinement (experiment A): bumped the soft-scale cooldown from 20s -> 35s for GPU-backed dedicated pools to reduce oscillation observed during short bursts. Early signal: fewer transient container churn events, but slightly longer time to reach full capacity for sustained surges. Owner: Diego (PLAT-3421).
- Per-route QoS tagging: started tagging a subset of low-latency routes with priority=high to bias allocator selection. This is a staged experiment; currently only request headers from OSS-inference-demo are tagged. Owner: Priya.
- Auth validator tolerant mode: added a whitelist for unknown string claims to prevent token rejections while we engage partner X. This is flagged in logs for follow-up auditing. Owner: Samir.

Decisions and follow-ups (action items):
- AI-1 (Diego) PLAT-3421: finish autoscaler smoothing param sweep and run a long-tail burst sim by 2026-10-23. Include at least two multi-region burst profiles. Status: in progress.
- AI-2 (Priya) PLAT-3478: roll per-route QoS tagging to 20% of eligible routes after validating SLO impact in staging. Target date 2026-10-22. Blocker: need a metrics dashboard widget for per-tag latency.
- AI-3 (Samir): open a follow-up with partner X to confirm token claim contract and remove tolerant path by 2026-11-01. Also add a short audit job that surfaces tolerant-accepted tokens daily.
- AI-4 (Avery): write a short playbook for 429-driven retry storms (include suggested backoff config, circuit-breaker thresholds, and example ephemeral denial rules) and circulate to solutions-eng by 2026-10-20.

Notes to self / informal observations:
- The telemetry-route misrouting felt like a config-sanity gap: we need a preflight check that warns when telemetry routes are assigned to dedicated pools. Low-risk fix: add a CI lint that ensures routes with tag 'telemetry' have pool_type != 'dedicated' unless explicitly approved.
- Quota spikes are disproportionately caused by a small number of test suites that have old SDK behavior (no jitter on retry). We should prioritize SDK patches + publish a recommendation to partner teams.
- Rolling back the config was straightforward, but our rollback playbook is scattered across a few internal docs. I'll consolidate the rollback steps and add a one-pager.

Meeting notes (standup 2026-10-15, 09:30 PT):
- Quick sync attendees: Avery, Diego, Priya, Samir, Elena.
- Diego: autoscaler smoothing experiment status + request for more sim profiles.
- Priya: QoS tagging small rollout, needs dashboarding.
- Samir: auth tolerant path deployed in canary; requesting partner outreach.
- Elena: observed billing anomaly tied to telemetry misroute — filed support ticket with finance and added to PLAT-3499.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: tolerant auth path could mask a real token shape change and allow mis-issuance to go unnoticed. Mitigation: log sampling and daily audit job (AI-3).
- Risk: mis-tagging routes leads to capacity fragmentation. Mitigation: preflight lint and staged rollouts with guardrails.

Conversation threads / links referenced in the meeting:
- Allocator PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/612
- Autoscaler experiment ticket: PLAT-3421
- QoS tagging ticket: PLAT-3478
- Telemetry billing ticket: PLAT-3499

Unresolved questions / brainstorm items:
- Should we add an explicit "test-client" header that gets auto-throttled by allocator to avoid polluting production quotas? Pros: immediate separation. Cons: requires wide SDK adoption.
- Long-term: would a per-customer token-credit bank (soft credit cap that refills) reduce 429 cascades? Estimate work: medium; ask product for prioritization.

Attachments / artifacts to review before next sync:
- PLAT-3421 experiment notes (linked)
- Allocator PR #612 (linked)
- Draft playbook outline (in Drive) — path: shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/playbooks/retry-storm-playbook-draft.md

Next sync: quick check-in on 2026-10-22 09:30 PT to review autoscaler sim results and decide on QoS rollout expansion.

Quick closing note: keep an eye on the 4am UTC window next week — we still see bursty test runs around that time from one partner. If you see unusual quota noise, tag #platform-controlplane and drop a short note with request IDs so we can trace quickly.

-- Avery
